title: If the whistle blows, stop
source: T3 L1 facilitator card (Teach and Unplugged stations)
status: DRAFT. Hints adapted from the facilitator card wording. Need a teacher check. Sesotho fields are empty until a Sesotho speaker has written them.

done.en: Well done. Tell your partner another if-then rule from home or school.

exercises.title: The whistle rule
exercises.prompt: Write the soccer rule in one sentence. Start with If, and use the word then.

exercises.title: No whistle
exercises.prompt: Finish the rule for when there is NO whistle: "If there is no whistle, then ..."

swapped_if_then.desc: Puts the action in the IF part and the whistle in the THEN part.
en: IF is what happens first, the signal. THEN is what we do about it.
Which part of your sentence is the whistle? Point to it. Is that the IF or the THEN?
Start again with: If the ___ , then we ___ .

missing_then.desc: Sentence has no clear IF part and THEN part.
en: Does your sentence have an IF part and a THEN part? Point to each.
What do the players do when the whistle blows?
Write it like this: If the whistle blows, then ... What do you do?

wrong_then.desc: THEN part is not what players do when the whistle blows.
en: Act it out. The whistle blows. What do you do?
What is the rule on the soccer field when the referee blows?
The players ... when the whistle blows. Finish that sentence.

stops_anyway.desc: Says players stop even when there is no whistle.
en: What did you do when there was no whistle?
If there is no whistle, does the rule tell you to stop?
No whistle means nothing tells you to stop. What do you keep doing?

no_match.desc: Answer does not say what happens without the whistle.
en: What happens on the field when there is no whistle?
Walk on the spot. No whistle. What are you doing?
Finish it with what the players keep doing: If there is no whistle, then ...

generic.desc: Any answer the coach cannot place.
en: Try again slowly. What does the exercise ask you to do first?
Say the first step out loud. What comes next?
Ask your partner what they think. If you are still stuck, ask your facilitator.
